articleTitle: Design of an Intelligent Lock Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: To address the problem of unlocking failures in intelligent locks due to power shortage or emergencies, this design uses the STM32FI03C8T6 as the main control chip. The system integrates fingerprint recognition, fire detection, facial recognition, mobile phone Bluetooth control, hand-crank power generation, and SOS emergency calling. By modifying the outdoor handle into a micro-generator handle, mechanical energy can be converted into electrical energy in emergencies to unlock the door. The system also includes gas and fire detection systems for emergency unlocking and an SOS system for emergency assistance, effectively preventing injuries and fatalities. The intelligent lock control system supports face recognition, fingerprint recognition, emergency alarms, hand-crank power generation, and password unlocking functions.

articleTitle: Study on Thermal Resistance Performance of Press-Pack IGBT Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: As an emerging power electronic device, Press-Pack IGBTs (PP-IGBT) are widely used in high-voltage DC transmission applications, but the thermal resistance modeling and parameter analysis of such devices are still unclear. This paper takes the 4500V/800A PP-IGBT module produced by SIMO as an example, disassembles and measures the module, establishes an Ansys analysis model, for the finite element method analysis of the influence of each surface heat dissipation on the thermal resistance results and temperature distribution of the module. Based on the simulation results, and experimental verification is conducted.

articleTitle: Vehicle Overload Warning Method Based on GNSS Displacement Signals of Long-Span Bridges
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: The deflection response can intuitively express the influence of bridge vehicles on the structural deformation, which is usually used as an important basis for evaluating the bearing capacity of long-span bridge structures. Firstly, the frequency-domain characteristics of vehicle-induced quasi-static displacement responses within the corresponding allowable highway speed are obtained by the transient finite element analysis. Using the adaptive variational mode decomposition and the time window technique, the live-load periods (i.e. the quasi-static response range) and the dead-load periods are accurately separated from the original Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) vertical displacement signal. By analyzing the displacement signal during the dead-load periods, the statistical time-domain characteristics of the GNSS multipath effect can be acknowledged. Then the warning limits of the GNSS deflection signal are obtained. Finally, the proposed vehicle overload warning method is validated by a 660m-long suspension bridge.

articleTitle: Anti-Aging Row Redundancy Technology of SRAM Based on New 12T Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: In this paper, in order to alleviate the aging of SRAM caused by NBTI, an anti-aging row redundancy technology is proposed. Redundant rows are added to the original array to make each row take turns to rest to restore the threshold voltage. Based on the reaction-diffusion model, the relationship between the number of redundant rows and the service life of the array in the worst case is derived. Because the traditional 6T cell is an interlocking structure, the threshold voltages of two PMOS cannot be restored at the same time. A new 12T cell is designed, in which the threshold voltages of two PMOS can be restored at the same time during the rest period, and the storage values can be directly transferred between rows without reading and writing when switching working rows.

articleTitle: Research on Hardware Acceleration Technique for Weight-Based Fixed Pulsed Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of deep neural networks, their model size and computational volume are getting larger and larger, and there are often problems such as power consumption and latency when they are used in embedded applications. To address these problems, ping-pong operation, data fixed-point quantization, and weight-fixed pulsed array hardware acceleration methods are proposed to solve these problems. In this paper, the LeNet-5 model algorithm is taken as an example for hardware acceleration design implementation. Finally, the performance is evaluated by performing on a heterogeneous Xilinx Zynq-7000 platform. The results from the experiment demonstrate a notable 20-fold boost in speed achieved by the custom accelerator outlined in this study when compared to the performance of a CPU. Additionally, in terms of energy efficiency, the custom accelerator significantly outperforms both the CPU by 1.3 times and the GPU by an impressive 26-fold margin.

articleTitle: Random Interpolation Average Using Lifting Scheme for Signal Denoising
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: In order to improve the denoising effectiveness of the random interpolation average (RIA) scheme, the lifting scheme was applied for signal denoising in this paper. The proposed method can obtain satisfying denoised results and keep the computational load at a proper level. Numerical results showed that the process in this paper supplies the best signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and root of mean square error (RMSE). In comparison to the classical wavelet transforms (WT), the conventional lifting scheme (LS), and the fully translation-invariant (TI) scheme, the RIA scheme has shown a significant improvement in the average signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of denoised signals, with increases of 3.21 dB, 3.82 dB, and 0.68 dB, respectively. According to the visual results, the singular points of four signals can be kept very well without introducing considerable distortion.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of 3-Zone Step Doping Junction Termination Extension for 20kV 4H-SiC Thyristor
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: A 20 kV 4H-SiC thyristor with 3-zone step doping junction termination extension is investigated in this paper. The simulation results show that the breakdown voltage of the thyristor terminated with step doping JTE can achieve 23 kV, corresponding efficiency is about 95.64%. Gaping and overlaying in the two-nested ion implantation process of three-zone JTE will lead to the surface electric field to higher. The peak of the surface electric field in the gaping case and the overlaying case are 2.13 MV/cm and 1.73 MV/cm are higher than the 1.36 MV/cm under the ideal situation. Therefore, it is necessary to strictly control the lithography process deviation to avoid gaping and overlaying situations to prevent electric field spikes within the JTE.

articleTitle: Analysis of Smart Substation Relay Protection Debugging and Application
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: With the continuous growth of social demand for electricity, the number of power engineering projects is also rising steadily. The progress of science and technology has promoted the smart substation to become the frontier trend of substation construction. The construction of smart substation involves many advanced technologies, including but not limited to digital transformer, network communication technology, photoelectric technology, etc. These technologies not only change the structure and function of the substation, but also aim to ensure that the substation can achieve sustainable, stable, safe and economical operation. Therefore, the relay protection system of smart substation has become a key topic in the research field. This paper will discuss the debugging process and its application of relay protection in smart substation.

articleTitle: Design of the Miniaturization of Bandpass Filter Based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: The realization of minimized filter with different shapes of slots on the surface of square substrate integrated waveguide filter (SIWF) is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the principle of square SIWF and the design of a dual passband square SIWF with a passband of 9.30 GHz to 9.82 GHz and 15.26 GHz to 16.58 GHz are introduced. The simulations of four SIW filters with different slots are presented in this paper. The comparison among four filters verifies the miniaturization of the proposed bandpass filter based on SIW.

articleTitle: Study on the Characteristics of 3.5kV Buried FS Layer Pulse Thyristor
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: Pulse thyristors have found wide applications in the field of pulsed power technology due to their high peak current and high voltage withstand capabilities. However, traditional round pulse thyristors are constrained by process conditions. During turn-on, the relatively slow two-dimensional expansion speed of carriers can lead to local overheating and subsequent device failure under high di/dt conditions due to current concentration. Additionally, specific application scenarios require pulse thyristors to possess a certain level of reverse voltage withstand capability. This paper proposes a square pulse thyristor with an embedded FS layer and conducts simulation studies on key parameters affecting device characteristics. The results indicate that increasing the cathode width <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{N}^{+}}$</tex> and cell width <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{W}_{\text{cell}}$</tex> is beneficial for reducing the on-state voltage drop, and increasing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{N}^{+}}$</tex> is conducive to enhancing the peak current. However, excessively large <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{N}^{+}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{W}_{\text{cell}}$</tex> can result in uneven current distribution beneath the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}^{+}$</tex> cathode region. Reducing the subsurface concentration <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{N}}{ }^{+}{}_{-}\text{Pbase}$</tex> in the P-base region aids in decreasing the on-state voltage drop, but excessively low <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{N}}{ }^{+}{}_{-}\text{Pbase}$</tex> can adversely affect the device's forward voltage withstand capability. The concentration of the FS layer (NFS), the thickness of the N2-base region <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{N}2^{-}})$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{N}}{ }^{+}{}_{-}\text{Pbase}$</tex> all positively correlate with the device's turn-on delay time. The minority carrier lifetime influences the device's blocking characteristics, conduction characteristics, and pulsed discharge characteristics, with a positive correlation observed. In practical processes, gettering techniques can be employed to maximize the minority carrier lifetime, thereby ensuring optimal device characteristics.

articleTitle: Research on Temperature Calibration of Fiber Bragg Grating Temperature Sensor Based on BPNN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: Temperature calibration of fiber bragg grating (FBG) temperature sensor is of vital importance to measuring accuracy, especially in varying temperature conditions. To improve the measurement accuracy of the FBG temperature sensor, a new algorithm which adopts BP neural network (BPNN) to temperature calibration of FBG temperature sensor is proposed and analyzed. In this study, we illustrate the principle of FBG temperature sensing. To verify the performance of the proposed temperature calibration method based on BPNN algorithm, a series of calibration experiments under -55°C, -30°C, -5°C, 20°C, 45°C and 70°C were implemented. Comparison fitting results of polynomial fitting method and BPNN algorithm verified the BPNN algorithm could fit better the relationship between the wavelength of FBG and ambient temperature. The sum of squares due to error, mean squared error and root mean squared error are 0.0036 nm2, 5.9887 e-04 nm and 0.0244 nm in fitting result of FBG _ Tl sensor and 0.0024 nm2, 4.0096e-04 nm and 0.0199 nm in fitting result of FBG _ T2 sensor which proved the significant effectiveness of BPNN algorithm.

articleTitle: Modulation Signal Recognition of Small Sample Radar Based on Attention Mechanism Prototype Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: In the modern battlefield environment, the signals of new radar systems are often short of enough samples to train deep learning models. At the same time, hostile parties may use various jamming and spoofing techniques, resulting in an extremely complex radar signal environment. In this case, how to quickly and accurately identify enemy radar signals is of vital significance for the acquisition of electronic countermeasures and air superiority. In this paper, a channel attention-mechanism module (Squeezed and Excitation Network) is introduced to improve the prototype network. By explicitly modeling the interdependence between convolutional feature channels, SE-Net can make the network pay more attention to important feature channels. The time-frequency images of thirteen kinds of LPI radar signals are extracted, and prototype network training based on attention mechanism is carried out to improve the prototype network by optimizing the mapping of embedded space and the design of classifier, which can further improve the accuracy and efficiency of radar signal recognition in the case of small samples. According to the simulation results, when the training set is only 8 classes and the test set is 13 classes, the recognition accuracy of SE-protonet network can reach 85% at OdB signal-to-noise ratio, which is 2 % higher than the pure protonet network and 20% higher than the traditional neural network, and has a good recognition accuracy at -12c <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> SdB signal-to-noise ratio. At the same time, when the number of support set samples reaches 15-shot, the recognition rate of 8dB signal to the whole signal can reach 98%. This further shows that the attention-mechanism-based prototype network has a good recognition accuracy for radar modulated signals in the case of small samples, and performs well in multi-class signal recognition and dynamic signal environment adaptation.

articleTitle: Preparation of Bumps Using a Novel Photosensitive Conductive Polymer Material for Micro-LED Display Application
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: Micro-light-emitting diode (Micro-LED) is increasingly favored due to their significant advantages in the performance of emerging augmented reality (AR) or virtual reality (VR) displays. A key process of single-chip integration technology in high-density micro displays is the interconnection process, which is closely related to the quality of display devices. The traditional chip interconnection is mainly achieved by preparing metal-based bump, which requires metal evaporation after photolithography, increases the process flow complexity, and poses a risk of photoresist peeling off. To solve these problems, we use a new type of photosensitive conductive polymer material to prepare bump that has conductivity and can directly interconnect chips vertically. Therefore, this method can eliminate the process of metal evaporation and reduce experimental risks. The results indicate that by optimizing the process parameters, bumps with high uniformity can be successfully prepared. This material can simplify the process flow and improve the success of subsequent vertical interconnection steps.

articleTitle: Research on Weak Signal Processing Methods for Electrical Imaging Logging Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: Using the actual formation resistivity and porosity spectrum information, the electroimaging tool can quickly estimate the oil content of complex reservoirs, and can recognize the sedimentary structure and micro-cracks in tight oil and gas reservoirs by improving the measurement accuracy of the instrument. For electrical imaging logging, improving the detection accuracy of weak signals is a necessary condition for enhancing the quality of logging data, improving imaging resolution, and making imaging clearer. In response to the problem that current processing algorithms for electrical imaging logging signals cannot guarantee complete signal information while denoising, this paper establishes a logging noise signal analysis model based on the characteristics of logging signals, and uses wavelet transform and three adaptive LMS filtering algorithms to process the model. Simulation experiments on MATLAB show that the maximum mean square error of the adaptive LMS algorithm is greatly reduced than that of the wavelet method, which shows that the method has better filtering performance. Among the three adaptive LMS algorithms, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1/2\text{LMS}$</tex> algorithm has the fastest running speed and the lowest MSE value, making it the most suitable for measuring weak signals underground.

articleTitle: Design of Current Mode CMOS Multiplication Circuits Based on Trans-Linear Loops
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: In this paper, a low-power, high-precision current mode CMOS multiplication circuit design method is proposed. Using the square characteristic of NMOS operating in the saturation region to form a trans-linear loop, the multiplication square term equation can be derived, and on this basis, the multiplication circuit and division circuit are designed. The multiplication circuit is also combined with the power expression of the logic function to complete the design of the basic current mode CMOS logic gate circuit, which constitutes the complete set. Simulation is performed using Pspice under 180nm CMOS process parameters, and verification of the circuit shows that the power consumption of the multiplication circuit is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0. 333\mathrm{W}$</tex>, linearity error is 0.8%, full harmonic distortion THD 1.59%, the circuit structure is simple, the results show that the circuit has low power consumption and high accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of Data Encryption and Decryption IP Core Based on SATA Host Transport Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: As data storage and information leakage issues become increasingly severe, hard drives face various potential security threats. To address the urgent need for secure data transmission and encryption protection, this paper, based on the SATA III protocol and information security technology, innovatively proposes an encryption/decryption IP core design for the SATA host-end transmission layer. By analyzing the SATA data structure and process, the layout of the host-end transmission layer is optimized, incorporating an encryption/decryption IP core compatible with the SM4 algorithm to ensure data security during transmission and storage in SATA devices. Using Verdi tools and a UVM-based verification environment for simulation testing and analysis, the proposed solution controls delay within 0.00008ms, demonstrating the feasibility and excellent performance of integrating encryption/decryption modules in the host-end transmission layer.

articleTitle: Study on the Breakdown Characteristics of SiC LDMOS with P-Upper Region
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: The junction terminal structure is extensively utilized in power electronics due to its substantial ability to enhance breakdown voltage. In this study, utilizing Silvaco TCAD semiconductor device simulation software, we optimally design a SiC LDMOS device incorporating a P-upper region. Initially, the simulation structure of the device is presented. Subsequently, we explore the impact of various parameters, including the spacing between the left side of the P-upper region and the P-body region, the spacing between the right side of the P-upper region and the drain region, the junction depth of the P-upper region, and the doping concentration, on the device's voltage resistance characteristics. Furthermore, the breakdown mechanism is analyzed in terms of surface electric fields, longitudinal electric fields, and peak electric fields. The results indicate that, with a constant doping concentration in the drift region, the breakdown voltage initially decreases and then increases with the reduction of the right-side spacing, while the breakdown voltage on the left-side spacing exhibits a linear relationship. When the left-right spacing is fixed, the breakdown voltage first decreases and then increases with the increase of P-upper junction depth and doping concentration. Comparing these results, it is evident that the optimized P-upper structure in the SiC LDMOS device achieves a more uniform surface electric field distribution, leading to enhanced device reliability and stability.

articleTitle: Design and Test of Missile-Borne Acquisition and Storage System for Magnetoelectric Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: The magnetoelectric sensor can solve the problem of acceleration sensor signal adhesion when a large aspect ratio warhead penetrates a multi-layer protective structure at high speed to certain extent, but no missile-borne acquisition and storage system suitable for this sensor has been found. Therefore, this paper designed a magnetoelectric sensor missile-borne acquisition and storage system, which used GD32E230K8T6 as the main control chip, used the on-chip SAR-ADC to realize the analog-to-digital conversion, and used a resistor network to realize the in-phase attenuation linear transformation for the signal. The data was stored in a 256Kbit FRAM with a sampling rate of more than 100kHz and a sampling accuracy of 12bit. The test result showed that the prototype accomplished the acquisition task and the storage task, and had power-off protection with 330ms working time after power-off. The prototype can meet the requirements of missile-borne acquisition and storage.

articleTitle: Multiphysics Analysis on 2.5D Chiplet Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: In recent years, as Moore's Law is approaching its physical limit, chiplet technology as a solution that can extend Moore's Law has been emphasized by the industry. However, there are still many problems with its widespread use. In this article, a 2.5D chiplet structure was built and then the structure was analyzed for coupled thermal-stress-electric multi-physical fields using COMSOL software. The following conclusions can be reached. 1) Due to the mismatch of the coefficients of thermal expansion of the materials, at high temperatures, the interface between the two materials will generate stresses, leading to warping of the entire structure and affecting the reliability of the structure. 2) Changes in the electromagnetic properties of materials caused by high temperatures lead to phenomena such as spectrum offset in devices placed on silicon interposer.

articleTitle: Back Gate Controlled Pseudo-P-Channel GaN HFET
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel pseudo-p-channel AlGaN/GaN heterostructure field-effect transistor (PP-HFET). As semiconductor technology advances, GaN devices are preferred for high-power and high-frequency applications due to their high electron mobility, breakdown field, and wide bandgap. Traditional AlGaN/GaN HFETs perform well because of their high electron density and mobility in the 2DEG channel. However, conventional n-type AlGaN/GaN HFETs are limited in applications requiring p-channel devices. The PP-HFET consists of a top reference electrode and a back-gate control electrode. During operation, the top reference electrode of the PP-HET is biased negatively, rendering the device to be initially in the off state. When a negative voltage is applied to the back gate, the two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) in the channel is regenerated owing to the compensation effect of the electric field. The more negative the back-gate voltage, the higher the ON current of the device, exhibiting the same characteristics as those of a p-channel device. The effects of the device parameters on the output and transfer characteristics are comprehensively examined, and an analytical model is presented. The simulation results illustrate that the threshold voltage of the proposed device based on the back-gate control is approximately -3.5 V, and the current density is as high as 0.1 A/mm, which is much higher than that of the conventional E-mode p-channel GaN HFET based on two-dimensional hole gas.

articleTitle: The Impact of Neutron Energy on Laser Simulation Technology in Transient Synergistic Damage
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: The study explores the impact of neutrons with different energies on laser simulation of silicon bipolar junction transistors (Si BJTs) under transient synergistic damage. By simulating the energy deposition distribution and transient current response of low-energy and high-energy photons at different neutron energies (ranging from 1 e V to 2 MeV), the following results are revealed: For high-energy neutron surroundings (energy > 100 keV), low-energy photons can effectively simulate high-energy photons to cause transient synergistic damage effects with neutrons. In contrast, for low-energy neutron surroundings (energy < 100 keV), the energy deposition distributions of low-energy and high-energy photons interacting with neutrons differ significantly. In other words, laser simulation techniques are suitable for studying transient synergistic damage of Si BJTs in high-energy neutron surroundings but have limitations in low-energy neutron surroundings. Therefore, the influence of neutron energy should be considered when applying laser simulation techniques to study transient synergistic damage.

articleTitle: A Novel Trench IGBT with Built-in Temperature Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: An innovative trench insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) with temperature sensing is proposed for effective on-line monitoring of the junction temperature. The temperature sensing is consisted by the P doped polysilicon region where the sense and ground terminals are separated on the two sides of it, sensor controlling gate and the oxide isolation part. It is easy fabricated with the conventional trench IGBT. Investigated by the technology computer-aided design (TCAD) tools, the sensing signal keeps a brilliant linear relationship with the maximum junction temperature. And the temperature difference between the sensing part and the hotspot is extremely low due to the built-in sensing structure. It has also been verified that the IGBT featuring novel temperature sensing could detect junction temperature change during the short circuit test. Besides that, as the sensing mode has been well developed, the power dissipation of the proposed temperature sensing structure is optimized. That provides a convenient use in the real power systems, which could be regarded as a superior method to monitor system temperature status.

articleTitle: Research on Reliability Issues of Gallium Oxide Power Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: This article focuses on the reliability of gallium oxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{Ga}_2\mathrm{O}_{3})$</tex> and its power devices, studying the reliability of gallium oxide power devices and mainly revolving around the solutions to the problems encountered in the process flow such as design and preparation of gallium oxide power devices. It introduces a variety of methods in detail to achieve the design of a new device structure and optimize the existing process, so as to meet the high requirements of material, equipment and operation in the device preparation process. The various methods introduced are used to solve the four most common problems in the performance optimization of gallium oxide power devices: p-type doping problems; electrical performance issues; normal device shutdown issues; thermal management issues. Through learning these methods, we can improve the existing processes.

articleTitle: Optimizing Analysis of $1.55\mu \mathrm{m}$ InGaAsP/InP Distributed Feedback Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: In order to optimize the high-speed electro-absorption modulated lasers for applications in the fiber optic communication and the data center systems, the epitaxial structure of the distributed feedback (DFB) laser with the InGaAsP/InP material was designed. In this article, PICS3D software was utilized to simulate the output power and the side-mode suppression ratio (SMSR) of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.55\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> DFB laser under various parameters, including the quantum well thickness, the quantum well barrier thickness, the number of quantum wells, and cavity length. The simulation results show that when the number of quantum wells is 8, the quantum well thickness is 6nm, and the quantum barrier thickness is 10nm, with the injection current of 100mA, the threshold current is 13mA, the output power is 32.5mW, and the side-mode suppression ratio is 46.7dB. Subsequently, the output power and the side-mode suppression ratio of the DFB laser are found to reach the optimal values under these conditions.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Underwater Acoustic Signal Acquisition and Display Software Based on PyQt5
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: In underwater target detection experiments, real-time signal processing and result display of collected underwater acoustic signal data are very important for the experiment. This paper has designed and implemented an underwater acoustic signal acquisition and display software based on PyQt5. This software can control the acquisition device to collect real-time underwater acoustic signal data received by active sonar, and perform relevant signal processing and result display on the data in real time. This software uses a serial port to achieve communication between the software and the acquisition device. It controls the acquisition device by calling the C++ dynamic link library provided by the acquisition device developer. The software obtains real-time underwater acoustic signal data from the acquisition device, and then performs relevant signal processing on the underwater acoustic signal data. The data processing results are displayed in the form of time-domain graphs, spectrograms, and target trajectory graphs. During the experiment, users can also save the experiment data in real time as needed, and replay these experiment data files as needed after the experiment. Through extensive practical testing, this paper has demonstrated that the software effectively achieves real-time acquisition, signal processing, and result display of underwater acoustic signals. It has the advantages of low code volume, high execution efficiency, strong stability, and good scalability.

articleTitle: A Design Method to Enhance the Short-Circuit ability of Planar Gate SiC MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel design method to enhance the short-circuit endurance of planar gate SiC MOSFET, investigated by the numerical simulation. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}+$</tex> source regions were placed intermittently in the orthogonal direction rather than a conventional stripe pattern source region, which reduces the average temperature of the unit cell and the saturation drain current (IDS,sat) during short-circuit event, avoiding thermal concentration effects, and thus preventing burnout. Compared to conventional SiC MOSFET that increase length of channel (Lch=0.8um) to improve short-circuit endurance, device simulation results show that the maximum saturation drain current under the short-circuit event of 800 V DC bus voltage of the proposed device is reduced by about 11.4%, the threshold voltage (Vth) is largely unperturbed, and the lower specific on-resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{(\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{n},\mathrm{s}\mathrm{p}})}$</tex> is reduced by about 5%. Additionally, it has been demonstrated that reducing the proportion of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}+$</tex> source region <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\gamma)$</tex>, within a certain range does not deteriorate the forward conduction voltage drop.

articleTitle: Effect Mechanism of Dynamic Avalanche on Turn-Off Behavior and Ruggedness of IGCT
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: By analytical analysis and TCAD device simulation, the physical mechanisms behind the dynamic avalanche and resulting current filament during IGCT turn-off are revealed. It is demonstrated that dynamic avalanche can greatly increase the turn-off time and loss of the device, and with the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha_{pnp}$</tex> increasing, the avalanche-generated current filament becomes stronger and moves slower, which will weaken the ruggedness of the device at the turn-off.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Effect of Contact Resistance on the Output Accuracy of Standard Signal Generating Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: The output signals of standard circuits often change due to the presence of contact resistance, resulting in a decrease in signal accuracy. Therefore, the study analyzes signal attenuation, distortion, power loss, and thermal noise caused by contact resistance in response to changes in contact resistance on the output accuracy of standard signal generating circuits. Using the system to receive the wireless standard signal generating circuit signal can analyze the effect of contact resistance on the signal. The results show that when the resistance of the resistance box is constant, the larger the contact resistance the worse the accuracy of the signal, of which the highest accuracy in the resistance size of Im <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega$</tex>, the accuracy of 94.35%. At the same time the different channels of the system also have an effect on the signal accuracy. Channell has the highest signal accuracy value, up to 91.85%. It can be seen that the contact resistance has a greater impact on the wireless standard circuit signal, the larger the resistance the worse the signal accuracy. It can be concluded that the use of systems or devices with lower contact resistance can effectively improve the accuracy of wireless signals. The study of the impact of the standard signal generating circuit output accuracy has a better guiding role.

articleTitle: Reliability Research of Gallium Oxide MOSFET Power Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: This research focuses on the reliability of gallium oxide MOSFET power devices. With the rapid development of power electronics technology, gallium oxide has become a research hotspot in the field of power devices due to its excellent material properties. However, its reliability issue has become a key challenge in practical applications. Through in-depth experimental analysis and theoretical research, we systematically investigated the performance changes of gallium oxide MOSFET under different working conditions, including the influence of factors such as temperature and voltage stress on the reliability of the device. This paper focuses on the reliability of gallium oxide MOSFET power devices. Combined with relevant references at home and abroad, by studying its thermal conductivity and P-type doping and epitaxy issues, the key factors affecting the reliability of the device are revealed, and corresponding improvement measures and optimization schemes are proposed.

articleTitle: Reliability Test in Severe Environments of 1700 V Discrete SiC MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: SiC MOSFET., as a representative of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>i<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>devices., has been widely used due to its advantages such as high switching speed and low switching losses. The long-term operational reliability of SiC MOSFET is currently a hot topic of research. This paper tests the static and dynamic characteristics of a batch of discrete 1700 V., 45 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{m}\Omega$</tex> SiC MOSFETs and subjects them to a series of laboratory simulations of harsh environmental conditions., verifying their reliability under severe environments.

articleTitle: Design and Compromise of RC-IGBT with High Voltage to Suppress Snapback
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: Compared with the fourth generation field stop trench insulated gate bipolar transistor, the reverse-conducting insulated gate bipolar transistor (RC-IGBT) has the advantages of low cost, small volume and high reliability, which is limited by the inherent rebound phenomenon in the semiconductor back surface process and conduction. In this paper, a high-voltage trench RC-IGBT is designed by process simulation, which is different from the mainstream low voltage in the market. The electrical characteristics are simulated and how to suppress the rebound phenomenon from the design of process parameters is studied. At the same time, the influence of process parameters on the dynamic and static performance of the device is analyzed, and finally a set of process parameter schemes with low loss, high reliability and compromise performance is given.

articleTitle: Optimizing Deterministic Computing-Network Integration with TSN and Edge Computing Using MOGWO
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) and deterministic edge computing to meet the stringent requirements for low latency, high reliability, and deterministic communication in industrial control networks. We propose a novel solution that utilizes the Multi-Objective Grey Wolf Optimizer (MOGWO) algorithm to optimize network and computing resources in task processing. By combining TSN's Time-Aware Shaper (TAS) gate control list configuration with the edge computing cache queue allocation strategy, this study aims to achieve coordinated and integrated deterministic computing-network services. The system optimizes delay, jitter, and packet loss for high-priority tasks, ensuring timely transmission and computation. Results demonstrate that this approach significantly enhances the reliability and efficiency of industrial networks, providing a robust framework for deterministic services in critical applications and underscoring the importance and potential of deterministic computing-network integration.

articleTitle: Research on Anti-EMI Capability of Current Steering Logic CMOS Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: With the rapid development of technology, electromagnetic radiation has become universal but fatal to circuits. Circuits stabilities against EMI has become a major sign to judge circuits designing. In this paper, by using theoretical analysis and real circuit testing methods, it is proven that the current steering logic CMOS circuits has stronger anti-electromagnetic interference (anti-EMI) capabilities than traditional voltage CMOS circuits. Firstly, using field-line coupling theory, current signals in transmission lines are proven to be less easily interfered by electromagnetic radiation than voltage signals, which indicates its stronger anti-EMI capability than voltage signal in the line, theoretically. Further, NAND gate and quaternary counter PCB circuits were made for both current steering logic CMOS and voltage CMOS circuit. Using the Tesla coil and vector network analyzer (VNA) as electromagnetic radiation source respectively, we verified that current steering logic CMOS circuit has stronger anti-EMI capability than voltage CMOS circuit. By using ZNB20 VNA and standard gain antenna for electromagnetic radiation output, current steering logic CMOS circuits can keep functional under stronger electromagnetic radiation than voltage CMOS circuits. The maximum radiation power for current steering logic CMOS circuits to keep functional is up to hundreds of times more than the voltage CMOS circuits. Thus, compared with voltage CMOS circuits, current steering logic CMOS circuits are more suitable to work under strong electromagnetic environment.

articleTitle: Application of Improved Radix-2 FFT Algorithm in Lateral Logging
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: Array lateral logging technology is currently a hot topic in electrical logging research. How to accurately and quickly extract signal amplitudes from various frequency points of mixed signals is a prerequisite for achieving accurate calculation of formation resistivity. Digital Phase Sensitive Detection (DPSD) and Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) are the two most common digital detection methods in lateral logging tools. A new improved method is proposed to address the issue of long computation time in the reverse order process of the commonly used Reed algorithm in radix-2 FFT. Experimental results have shown that the improved FFT calculation speed is approximately 7 times faster than the conventional radix-2 FFT, and compared to the original method, the improved algorithm has doubled the computation speed; In terms of accuracy, DPSD performs better than traditional FFT in the absence of phase difference. However, as the phase shift increases, the change in dynamic phase difference will significantly increase. However, the improved FFT results are not affected by phase difference. By comparing and analyzing the two methods, it is proven that the resistivity curve obtained by FFT has better consistency and is suitable for measuring high resistivity formations <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(100000 \Omega\cdot \mathrm{m})$</tex>. Thus, the measurement accuracy of the instrument has been improved, providing more reliable data for the precise identification of oil and gas reservoirs.

articleTitle: Investigation of SiC MOSFET Based on Implantation for Anti-Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: This study investigates the anti-irradiation characteristics of SiC MOSFETs using multi-energy ion implantation. By simulating boron ion implantation in SiC with Sentaurus TCAD software and comparing the results with SIMS measurements, the reliability and stability of the devices were enhanced. The findings demonstrate that multi-energy implantation achieves uniform doping, improving anti-irradiation capabilities and reducing defect concentration, offering valuable insights for optimizing SiC MOSFET processes.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Wave Propagation Characteristics over Random Rough Sea Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: The rough sea surfaces significantly impact the scattering of electromagnetic waves within marine evaporation ducts, adversely affecting the accuracy and reliability of radar or optical remote sensing technologies. This paper addresses the influence of rough sea surface contours on electromagnetic wave propagation within marine evaporation ducts and proposes a computational method for electromagnetic wave propagation in maritime duct environments. This method integrates the scattering characteristics of rough sea surfaces and the impact of sea surface geometry, allowing for more accurate simulation of electromagnetic wave propagation over rough sea surfaces within marine evaporation ducts. The proposed method extends the existing rough sea surface Miller-Brown model by incorporating a terrain-like model to account for the wave shape's masking effect on electromagnetic waves. It begins by selecting the Elfouhaily sea spectrum model, using linear superposition to simulate a three-dimensional sea surface and calculating a two-dimensional ocean profile, followed by the parabolic equation method to simulate electromagnetic wave propagation over rough sea surfaces in evaporation ducts. Simulation results indicate that with increasing wind speed, the wave contour's blocking effect on electromagnetic waves intensifies, leading to increased propagation loss. Compared to the traditional Miller-Brown model, considering wave contour interference results in a 20dB increase in propagation loss at corresponding positions.

articleTitle: A Novel SPICE Modeling Approach for SiC D-MOSFET Based on BSIM3HV
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: SiC MOSFETs have emerged as a highly promising solution for power electronics applications due to their superior material properties, including a wide bandgap, high thermal conductivity, high critical electric field strength, and high saturation velocity of charge carriers. Accurate compact modeling of SiC D-MOSFETs is crucial when designing analog circuits for applications such as solar inverters, motor drives, high-voltage DC-DC converters, and uninterruptible power supplies (UPS). The current characteristics of SiC MOSFETs can be numerically assessed using TCAD simulation, which compares them against measurements from the device datasheet. In this paper, we present a comprehensive modeling approach for the SCT50N120 1200V SiC D-MOSFET from STMicroelectronics. The well-established industry-standard B<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex>IM3HV SPICE model is employed, and its key parameters are optimized to achieve an accurate fit between the simulated and measured current characteristics. This optimization process yields an refined SPICE circuit simulation model for the targeted SiC D-MOSFET device, which is subsequently verified through simulations. Ultimately, we demonstrate reasonable agreement between the optimized SPICE model simulations and the measured datasheet results for the IDS- VGS and IDS-VDS characteristics across various bias conditions.

articleTitle: Design and Characteristics Analysis of Electromagnets Based on ANSYS Maxwell
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: Electromagnets serve as key control components in polishing machines, critical for automating the polishing process. Their electromagnetic characteristics directly influence the control precision of the polishing head and the uniformity of the polishing effect. This paper fields to establish a mathematical model. Using ANSYS Maxwell's static magnetic field simulation, we obtained the force-air gap characteristic curves under various parameters of the electromagnet. The simulation results demonstrate that the number of ampere-turns should consider factors such as the stroke of the electromagnet and the magnetic induction strength of the material to avoid magnetic saturation. When the shell wall thickness is less than 7 mm, the static electromagnetic force decreases as the shell thickness decreases; The electromagnetic force at 7 mm and 8 mm is almost the same. Appropriately reducing the shell thickness, without compromising the structural strength or the performance of the electromagnet, aids in achieving lightweight and high power density electromagnets. The electromagnetic force increases with the radius of the iron core, but once the required electromagnetic attraction force is satisfied, the size of the iron core should be minimized to reduce the weight of the electromagnet. These simulation results can provide reference for the structural design and operational characteristics analysis of electromagnets, significantly shortening the design and development cycle of electromagnets.

articleTitle: Characteristic Analysis of 200V 4H-SiC RESURF LDMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: The characteristics of 200V 4H-SiC RESURF LDMOS is analyzed by simulation in this paper. The RESURF principle is adopted to shift the high field intensity of from the lateral pn- junction near the surface to the vertical p-n- junction in the body, so that the breakdown point is shifted from the surface to the bulk to increase the breakdown voltage. By optimizing the doping concentration and thickness of the n- drift region to make the surface electric field distribution uniform, can obtain the better trade-off between breakdown voltage and on-resistance.

articleTitle: A Depletion-enhanced N Layers Stacked LDMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: With the development of power integrated circuits, LDMOS devices assume a significant role in power device applications due to their elevated input impedance and enhanced conversion rate. Nonetheless, a contradictory relationship exists between the breakdown voltage and specific on-resistance in power LDMOS devices. Consequently, an n-layer stacked lateral double-diffused metal-oxide-semi conductor transistor(SLDMOS) is proposed, in which numerous MOS cells are stacked under the same chip area. The on-state resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{n}})$</tex> of the n layers S-LDMOS is decreased significantly because of the vertical parallel connection, also the interference among devices is weakened through electrode interconnection isolated by oxidation layer. Multiple drift regions are formed by alternate epitaxy N-layer (drift region) and P-layer (substrate), and each drift region is depleted by the top and bottom P substrates, leading to a much lower <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{n}}$</tex>. The lightly-doped substrate and N/P top region are used to improve the breakdown characteristics, and the floating P layers are introduced to enhance the depletion effect in drift regions and decrease device thicknesses. By optimizing the configuration, a balanced trade-off is obtained. The simulation results indicate that compared with the traditional LDMOS, the 2 layers S-LDMOS exhibits a BV of 356 V and a specific on resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{n},\mathrm{s}\mathrm{p}})$</tex> of 13.56 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\mathrm{m}\Omega\cdot \text{cm}^{2},}$</tex> an improvement of 26.2 % and 71.6%, respectively. And the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{n}}$</tex>, sp of n layers S-LDMOS will be reduced to less than 1/n of C-LDMOS further.

articleTitle: Research on a Device for Fluorescence Imaging Detection of Nucleic
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: With the rapid development of nucleic acid molecule detection technology, nucleic acid detection devices have become a global research hotspot in recent years. This paper uses multidisciplinary fusion technology to propose a nucleic acid fluorescence detection design scheme. The device is mainly composed of a motion module and an optical system. Among them, the motion module uses an S-type variable acceleration control method to precisely control the movement of the motor. The stable and accurate operation lays the foundation for the collection of fluorescent signals; the optical system uses LED as the fluorescent excitation light source. The LED collimated uniform light path is designed. Use image stitching to stitch the collected images into a complete image for analysis. Finally, measure the operating error of the motor, the average error does not exceed 14um; simulate the fluorescence signal acquisition system and collect the image of the fluorescent film, the image fluorescence is uniform, which verifies the rationality of the fluorescence acquisition system; collects simulated samples and blank control images, Analyze the stitched images, and the results clearly distinguish the simulated samples and the control group.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Layer Classification and Identification of Graphene 2D N Anosheets
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: With the development of technology, the application of two-dimensional nanosheets has become increasingly widespread, particularly in the fields of materials science, nanotechnology, and electronic engineering, where the precise identification of graphene layers is of paramount importance. Nowadays, there are many ways to explore 2D material nanosheets in the field of materials science, but there is still the problem that the average target detection accuracy is not high at different categories and thresholds. Therefore, to solve this problem, this paper proposes a deep learning-based object detection method for different classes of graphene two-dimensional nanosheets. The accurate value of the method is 99.12%, and some performance indicators of the algorithm are also improved compared with the classical algorithm. According to the results, the algorithm has better advantages for graphene nanopayer classification.

articleTitle: Effect of Incident Energy on Deposition of Ge0.2Si0.8 Films on Ge Substrate: A Molecular Dynamics Study
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: Due to its excellent electronic and optical properties, Ge/GeSi substrates have significant potential for application in the development of integrated circuits and optoelectronic devices. This article uses molecular dynamics simulation to study the effect of incident energy on the surface morphology, lattice structure, and dislocation distribution of Geo.2Sio.8 thin films deposited on Ge substrates. Research has found that incident energy can improve the surface smoothness of thin films and reduce their surface roughness. The increase in incident energy can also lead to intensified mixing at the interface between the substrate and the thin film. At the same time, the increase in energy can also reduce the proportion of amorphous in the film, reduce the formation of dislocations and other defects, and improve the overall quality of the film. However, excessive incident energy can cause deposited atoms to penetrate the substrate, disrupting its internal stability.

articleTitle: A Novel 3.63–V 6.73-ppm/°C CMOS Bandgap Reference
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: This paper presents a novel bandgap reference (BGR). Nine pairs of bipolar transistors are used to produce a voltage that is proportional to absolute temperature (PTAT), and three base-emitter voltages of bipolar transistors are used to produce a voltage that is complementary to absolute temperature (CTAT). The BGR of this structure can obtain a lower temper-ature coefficient with first-order temperature compensation. In the simulation, a voltage reference of 3.63 V with a temperature coefficient of 6.73 ppm/vC is achieved for a temperature range of - 45°C to 125°C at a 5 V supply voltage.

articleTitle: Multi-Dimensional Automatic Perception of Vehicles Spontaneous Combustion
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: Hot weather is one of the common causes of spontaneous combustion in automobiles, especially in the hot summer months. Vehicles under the sun, the temperature inside and outside the car may quickly rise to extremely high levels, in this case, the car's electric circuit, oil circuit and the ignition point of the contents of the car greatly reduced, very easy to spontaneous combustion phenomenon. Auto spontaneous combustion not only threatens the safety of the people inside the car, but also causes serious damage to the surrounding environment and property. However, with the continuous progress of science and technology, the application of intelligent technology in various fields has become more and more extensive, and the prevention of spontaneous combustion of automobiles, which is a complex safety issue, can also be solved with the help of advanced technical means. In this paper, using the YOLO model for flame image detection and combining temperature and gas sensors, an effective and innovative intelligent automated system for preventing automobile spontaneous combustion is proposed.

articleTitle: Research on Miniaturized Base Station Antenna Used in 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: A certain type of small-sized dual-polarized base station antenna for 5G mobile communication is investigated. The antenna's fundamental structure includes a reflector, a radiating plate, a set of crossed dipoles, and two feeding baluns. the crossed dipoles and the microstrip feed line are printed on an FR4 substrate that is 0.8mm thick. The consequence tells that the antenna's working frequency was 3.0-4.2GHz. In the 3.0-4.2GHz frequency band, the return loss of the antenna was less than −10dB, the voltage standing wave ratio was less than 1.5, the port isolation was better than 29dB, the gain was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8.0\pm 0.3\text{dBi}$</tex>. The antenna measure is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.41\}_{0}\times 0.41\lambda\times 0.15\}_{0}, \lambda$</tex> being the wavelength of the center frequency. This antenna encompasses all of the N78 frequency band, and simple process leads to characteristics such as miniaturization and high gain. And the antenna possesses qualities like a straightforward process, miniaturization, and high gain, and is capable of offering potential uses for 5G miniaturized base stations.

articleTitle: Design of A Controllable and Adjustable Spread Spectrum Clock Signal Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: With the rapid development of the internet industry, higher demands are placed on the power management chips, the core drivers of electronic devices, with particular emphasis on reducing electromagnetic interference (EMI). Clock generators typically represent the largest contributors to EMI within power management chips. This paper presents a design of a controllable and adjustable spreading signal generator capable of operating under a low voltage power supply of 3V. The spreading function can be enabled or disabled via an external enable signal. When the spreading function is disabled, the converter operates in fixed frequency mode, whereas when enabled, it operates in spreading mode. The center frequency of the oscillator can be adjusted by varying external resistances, while the spreading range and depth can be tuned by adjusting external reference voltage and charging capacitance. Simulation results using CMOS 0.18um technology indicate that spreading technology widens the spectrum of the system output signal, distributing energy more uniformly across a wider frequency band, resulting in a 56% reduction in peak energy of the fundamental wave. By controlling the spreading function's switch, a trade-off can be made between EMI and output voltage stability to accommodate different application scenarios, thereby enhancing system immunity to interference and achieving efficient energy conversion and stable power output.

articleTitle: Effects of the Band Gap Width of Emitter Materials and the Front Surface of the Top Electrode on the Performance of TOPCon Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: The width of the top electrode of the battery can represent the metal coverage of the front surface of the solar cell, that is, the greater the width of the top electrode of the battery, the higher the metal coverage of the front surface of the battery. Therefore, in this work, by changing the width of the top electrode of TOPCon battery, the influence of metal coverage on the performance of the battery is explored. Considering the conversion efficiency of the battery and the actual production process, this paper thinks that 2 % metal coverage on the front surface is the most suitable. Subsequently, in order to reduce the optical limitation of the emitter and improve the overall efficiency of tunnel oxide passivation contact (TOPCon) solar cells, six kinds of emitter materials with different band gap widths are used to simulate the TOPCon solar cells: GaSb, polysilicon, InP, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CuO}_{2}$</tex>, AlAs and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CuAlO}_{2}$</tex>. The influence of the band gap width of emitter materials on the performance of solar cells and its potential mechanism are deeply discussed. The results show that with the increase of the band gap width of the emitter material, the short-circuit current density and filling factor increase at first, and then decrease, while the open-circuit voltage continues to increase, resulting in the overall conversion efficiency following the trend of initial increase and subsequent decrease. Among the six materials studied, Cu02 is the best emitter material, which provides the highest conversion efficiency of solar cells.

articleTitle: Study of Influence of HTGB and HTRB Tests on Parameters of 1200V SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: In recent years, SiC MOSFETs have been replacing Si IGBTs in large numbers in the 1200V power device market, and the application prospects are very promising. However, the reliability problem of SiC MOSFETs has become more serious. In many new applications, SiC MOSFET devices need to work in harsh environmental conditions, and therefore need to be tested for reliability. In order to study the reliability of the devices under electrical and thermal stresses for a long time, the 1200V SiC MOSFETs were tested for High Temperature Gate Bias (HTGB) and High Temperature Reverse Bias (HTRB), and the trends of their parameters with time were analyzed.

articleTitle: Impedance Modeling Method for Improving the Grid Stability of Grid-Forming Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: In the context of new energy generation, the application proportion of power electronic converters in the power system is constantly increasing, and the inertia and damping of the system are reduced, which leads to stability issues. This article focuses on the control strategy and stability analysis of grid-forming inverters, exploring different modeling and stability analysis methods. On this basis, this article adopts a virtual synchronous generator control strategy to determine the system topology structure of the grid-forming inverter. Then, a sequence impedance model of grid structured inverters based on virtual synchronous generators was established under three different inner loop control schemes, and the model was simplified. Furthermore, based on the established impedance model, stability analysis was conducted on the three-phase inverter grid-connected system.

articleTitle: Detection Methods of Series DC Arc Fault in Photovoltaic System Based on Three-Dimensional Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: The present series DC arc fault (SAF) detection methods of photovoltaic system depend on complex identification methods and too simple characteristic. To address this problems, a method of SAF fault characteristic analysis and detection based on three-dimensional feature fusion is proposed. Firstly, the experimental platform is built to collect the original normal current and DC arc fault signals. Thereafter the change rate of the mean value of the current and the difference between the maximum and minimum values of the current cycle are extracted as the characteristic in the time domain. And the time-frequency characteristic is extracted by variational mode decomposition. Subsequently, the three-dimensional fault arc feature space is constructed based on the time domain, frequency domain and time-frequency domain feature vectors. The boundary parameters of the fault space are determined by experiments, and the characteristic criterion is obtained. At last, DC arc fault detection is realized based on three-dimensional feature criterion. Finally, the accuracy of the proposed method is verified by experimental analysis.

articleTitle: Research on Breakdown Mechanism and Characteristics of 4H-SiC BJT with Trench-JTE Composite Termination
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: The trench-JTE composite termination is designed based on the basis of 4H-SiC BJTs, and which is formed by etching the base mesa and then using ion implantation. The breakdown mechanism and characteristics of trench-JTE composite termination are researched. And combined with the actual process, the key parameters, such as trench depth and the width, concentration and junction depth of the JTE region are optimized. The simulation results, when the trench etching depth is 2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, the concentration, width and junction depth of the JTE region is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 10^{17}\text{cm}^{-3},25$</tex> um and 0.8 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> respectively, the breakdown voltage of 4H-SiC BJTs with trench-JTE composite termination is 1956 V, the voltage withstand efficiency is 96.31%.

articleTitle: Pixel Sharing Based Design of High Signal-to-Noise Ratio Mixed Domain Time Delay Integration Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor Image Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: With the progress of science and technology, people have higher and higher performance requirements for image sensors. Enhancing SNR (Signal-to-Noise Ratio) has become one of the important issues in optimizing the performance of image sensors nowadays. A mixed-domain accumulation technique based on pixel-sharing TDI (Time Delay Integration) CMOS (Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor) image sensor was proposed in this paper. By adopting a signal accumulation technique combining two levels of charge-domain accumulation with low-noise pixel-sharing and eight levels of analog-domain accumulation for suppressing parasitics, sixteen levels of accumulation was realized. The design of the mixed-domain TDI CMOS image sensor is fabricated in the 55-nm CMOS technology with sixteen levels of accumulation and a 58.82 kHz line frequency. The SNR of 16-stage accumulation can be improved by 21.96dB after simulation verification.

articleTitle: Design of Low On-State Loss IGBT Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: In order to reduce the on-state loss of Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistors (IGBTs), a device cell structure with carrier storage (CS) layer trench type Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistors (CSTBTs) is designed in this paper. The substrate thickness, substrate resistivity, CS layer injection dose, trench depth, and trench width of the CSTBT were simulated and optimized using the Sentaurus TCAD. The cell structure parameters and process parameters of the device were determined by studying the effect of variation of each parameter on the performance of the device. Test results show that the designed device has low on-state loss and good performance.

articleTitle: Study on Properties of Microcavity Resonant Modes of GaN Based Hexagonal Photonic Crystals
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: This paper proposes a resonant microcavity structure with different size defect holes of GaN based hexagonal photonic crystal in the 440 nm blue band. The resonance and field distribution properties of the microcavity structure before and after the addition of different size holes in the central dielectric region of the photonic crystal were analyzed by simulation calculation. The correlation and operation mechanism between the microcavity structure and different structural parameters of the photonic crystal was studied, including the duty ratio of the periodic porosity region and the duty ratio of the central dielectric defect region. The influence of duty ratio on quality factor (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex>) and resonant wavelength of microcavity was discussed. The results show that the defect structure can be effectively formed by adding small size etching air holes in the central dielectric region of the photonic crystal, thus enhancing the localization properties of the field distribution modes of the microcavity. The relative intensity of the field distribution Mode2 is 45, and the quality factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q$</tex> is 3000. The research has theoretical significance for the design of GaN based blue band resonator with high performance.

articleTitle: Integrating Structures Residual and C_Inception with Data Augmentation to Improve the Performance of LeNet-5
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of insufficient generalization ability and low training efficiency of the current LeNet-5 model, this paper tries to improve the performance of the model from two aspects: model improvement and data enhancement. Firstly, based on LeNet-5, a new convolutional neural network C_LeNet-5 is formed by incorporating Residual structure and C_ Inception module. Secondly, MNIST is expanded to a new dataset C_ MNIST by data augmentation techniques such as brightness adjustment, gaussian noise injection, erasing, rotation, scaling and translation. Finally, the recognition performance of LeNet-5 and C_LeNet-5 on the C_MNIST dataset is compared, and the experimental results show that the C_LeNet-5 model performs better than the original model in handwritten digit recognition task. C_LeNet-5 model has stronger feature extraction ability, more stable training and faster convergence.

articleTitle: Optimization Design and Simulation of 1.2kV SiC Optically Controlled Transistor for Power Switch
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: An optimized design of a 1.2 kV SiC NPN optically controlled transistor was developed. By using the Sentaurus TCAD tool, the doping concentration and thickness of the p-base region, as well as the ratio of light window width to electrode width, were systematically designed and optimized to achieve an optimal trade-off between breakdown voltage and current gain. When the base region thickness is O.2μm, the concentration is 7x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sup> cm-3, and the ratio of light window width to electrode width is 19, the resulting breakdown voltage is 1476V, the current gain is 249.74AIW, and the transition frequency is 10MHz. These results indicate that the SiC NPN optically controlled transistor optimized using this method is suitable for high-voltage, high-frequency, and high-power applications.

articleTitle: Electrical Properties of Al2O3-Gate AlGaN/GaN MOSHEMTs: TMC and Size Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: Based on the charge control model, the electrical properties are studied in the AlGaN/GaN MOSHEMTs with Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> gate, considering the fixed chargers and the polarization in the nitride heterostructures. It is found that the threshold voltages will shift to the negative direction when each layer's thickness and Al component increase. The drain current rises obviously with increasing barrier thickness and Al component, whereas an opposite effect presents when the thickness of Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> gate increases. Meanwhile, the variations of Al component and devices' size have a significant influence on electron density. These results indicate that the electrical properties can be improved if the suitable values of Al component and film size are adopted in the fabrication of MOSHEMT devices.

articleTitle: Study on the Characteristics and Mechanism of High-Voltage 4H-SiC Dual-Mode Composite Transistor (DCT)
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of high on-resistance and poor short-circuit tolerance of 4H-SiC Vertical Double-diffusion MOSFET (VDMOS), a Dual-mode Composite Transistor (DCT) is proposed in this paper, and the static, switching and short circuit characteristics of DCT are studied and compared with VDMOS with current spread layer (CSL) by TCAD simulator. The results show that DCT has higher breakdown voltage, lower on-resistance and better short-circuit performance. When the operation frequency is less than 145kHz, the total power loss of DCT is less than VDMOS.

articleTitle: A Fast Transient Response Capacitor-Less LDO with Dual Transient Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: This paper proposes a capacitor-less LDO with fast transient response. A dual-regulated transient enhancement circuit is proposed, which includes an undershoot suppression circuit and an overshoot suppression circuit. The circuit detects changes in the LDO output voltage (dvout/dt) and converts the voltage change into a current that charges or discharges the power transistor gate and the LDO output directly without going through the error amplifier loop. Using a unipolar folded cascade operational amplifier to achieve high gain while simplifying the distribution of zeros and poles in the LDO loop. A dual cascade compensation structure is used to ensure that the LDO loop has sufficient phase margin under both heavy and light load conditions. At the same time, the compensation structure also provides a fast path from the LDO output to the power transistor gate. The dual-regulated transient enhancement circuit and dual-cascade compensation work together to suppress the overshoot and undershoot of the LDO output voltage caused by load current jumps, improving the transient response of the LDO.
