Capacitance-voltage (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C-V$</tex>) analysis measurement was utilized to characterize the oxide trapped charge density (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta N_{ot}$</tex>) and the interface trapped charge density (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta N_{it}$</tex>) before and after irradiation. Our experimental results show that i) the oxide trapped charge density (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta N_{ot}$</tex>) in the HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>MOS at 100 K is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.4\times 10^{12}cm^{-2}$</tex>, which is higher than the value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 10^{11}cm^{-2}$</tex> measured at 300 K; ii) the interface trapped charge density (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta N_{it}$</tex>) resulting from proton irradiation at 100 K is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 10^{11}cm^{-2}$</tex>, which is lower than the value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6\times 10^{11}cm^{-2}$</tex> measured at 300 K. The mechanism of the temperature effect on HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> MOS capacitors was investigated through Kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) simulations, which indicated that temperature decreasing can enhance the stability of charged defects in the oxide layer, facilitating the generation of oxide tapped charges. Besides, the temperature decreasing can reduce the interface trapped charges by suppressing hydrogen-related defect decomposition reactions. The assignment of how temperature affects the total ionizing dose effect in MOS capacitors is important to advance the understanding of complex processes occurring under ion-solid interactions, as well as in the design of aerospace MOS devices.

articleTitle: Multi-Variable Analysis of Current Carrying Characteristics and Solder Joint Thermal Stress in TSV Structures of Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: As ICs advance toward smaller dimensions and higher power densities, the current carrying characteristics of TSVs within ICs significantly impact their thermal behavior during operation. The thermal stresses lead to mechanical fatigue of the TSVs, degrading the performance and lifetime of the ICs. This paper focuses on the modeling of TSVs for integrated circuits, constructing an electro-thermo-mechanical multi-physics coupled model. Finite element simulations are employed to analyze the impact of TSV radius, height, quantity, and current on current carrying characteristics. Based on these analyses, the thermal stress induced by Joule heating is further investigated. The results demonstrate that TSV radius exerts the most significant influence on current carrying characteristics, with a unit change reaching 262.82%, followed by current density, which exhibits a unit change of 92.85%. Regarding thermal stress, TSV radius demonstrated the most substantial impact, with a unit change of 119.17%, while current density displayed the second most significant influence, with a unit change of 77.95<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>. TSV quantity and height showed unit changes of 56.55% and 55.32% respectively. The combination of smaller radius and higher currents accelerates thermal aging in TSVs, increasing the likelihood of structural failure and resulting in diminished performance and reduced lifespan for the ICs.

articleTitle: Study on the Electronic Properties of th-A1N Adsorption by Gases
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: The novel proposed two-dimensional tetrahex aluminum nitride (th-AIN) has the advantages of wide bandgap, indirect transition, high-temperature resistance, high stability, and high electron mobility. Because low dimensional materials with large specific surface areas are sensitive to the material surface, the electron adsorption properties of background air gases molecules O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, N2, CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$</tex> and polluted gases molecules SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, CO, and NO on th-AIN surface were studied, and the sensitivity and selectivity of material for gases were discussed using bonding, calculation of adsorption energy, energy band structure and density of states curve. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N2, \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}, CO2$</tex> and CH4 adsorption of th-AIN is physical adsorption and th-AIN with no significant change in band structure is not sensitive to it. O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, CO, NO, NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> adsorption of th-AIN is chemical adsorption, that causes the bandgap to decrease significantly, and th-AIN with a significant change in band structure has a certain degree of sensitivity to it. Meanwhile, O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> adsorption of th-AIN will cause the bandgap to decrease significantly, transforming the indirect-direct transition mode. Thus, th-AIN must isolate oxygen when used as the gas-sensing material. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{O}_{2}/\text{NO}/\text{NO}_{2}/\text{SO}_{2}+\text{AlN}$</tex> adsorption system all exhibit magnetism, with varying magnetic moments of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.68 \mu \mathrm{B}\sim 1.52\mu \mathrm{B}$</tex>. Some results of this study provide theoretical guidance for future design and synthesis of th-AIN gas sensing material.

articleTitle: Indoor Cooperative Localization Algorithm Based on UWB/PDR Data Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Semiconductor and Electronic Technology (ISSET)
abstract: In recent years, there is an increasing demand for indoor localization, and multi-source data fusion algorithms have gradually become a research hotspot. Ultra-wideband (UWB) technology is widely used for its high accuracy, but the effect decreases significantly in non-line-of-sight (NLOS) environments. Pedestrian Dead Reckoning (PDR) technology estimates step length and direction from sensor data, which has high localization accuracy in a short period of time, but the problem of error accumulation is serious with the increase of time. To address these problems, this paper proposes a nested Extended Kalman Filter (N-EKF) that fuses the ranging information of UWB with the step length and heading angle values of PDR to obtain the pedestrian position coordinates. The experimental results show that the fusion algorithm reduces the average error by 75% and 52.2% compared to the UWB and PDR localization algorithms, which effectively alleviates the excessive UWB ranging error in weak NLOS environments.
